Maria: FYI after the 11:30 deploy (commit c3f9a2b) we see a clear p99 spike for streaming endpoints — ~25% higher. Non-stream endpoints look stable. Tool-call latencies up by ~200-400ms per call.

Maria: Quick profiling snapshot (from staging reproduce):
```
# top hot paths (ms per request)
serialize_frame                 18.2  <- up from 3.4
toolcall_handshake              24.7  <- up from 5.1
write_chunk_padding             12.6  <- new, correlates with header change
kv_prefetch                     2.1
kernel_select                   1.0
```

Ajay: Reproduced locally with stress-runner 20k reqs/min, same shape. Suspect the eventstream framing change in PR 3124 that added a 4-byte padded header + conditional flush. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3124

Tyler: CI perf job "perf/integration/streaming-p99" failed on master in the last run — diff shows +27% p99. Build: 2026-03-18T11:15Z, job id 7744. Logs: `stream_writer.flush()` calls jumped.

perf-bot: Detected regression: streaming-p99 increased by 26% vs baseline (7 days). Suspected files: runtime/eventstream/writer.cpp, runtime/toolcall/handshake.rs

Sophia: Quick thought — we recently added a small-header path to support tool metadata. That path calls `writer.write(padded_header); writer.flush_if_needed()` which can turn many small writes into blocking syscalls. Could be TCP coalescing + Nagle interactions. Can someone run `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/esp.pcap` while reproducing and check packet sizes?

Kevin: If this is causing customer impact we should hold the rollout. I can open a revert PR. Will push revert for PR 3124 in 10m unless someone objects. Revert PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3130

Ajay: I'll run a bisect across commits from b9a4e00..c3f9a2b focusing on eventstream and toolcall files. Also will try toggling `stream_writer.tcp_nodelay` flag in staging to see delta.

Maria: Quick mitigation that doesn't require full revert: disable padded-header path behind feature flag (off by default) + fallback to previous header format. Will open a small PR for that so we can keep other changes.

Tyler: Note: kernel-select path is unaffected which points at serialization/IO hot path rather than model kernel logic. That matches the profile.

Sophia: Command I used to capture small-write pattern: `sudo tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/stream-headers.pcap port 443 and host staging-host` then open pcap in Wireshark and filter by `tcp.len == 0 or tcp.len < 100`. If we see lots of 1-2 packet small payloads, that's our culprit.

Maria: I'll run the pcap and attach in the bug. Also running `strace -tt -f -p <pid>` to confirm syscall timing for write/flush.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused for release/2026-03-18 after manual hold by Kevin.

Kevin: Revert PR created and tested locally; perf regressions gone when revert applied. Suggest we hold and ship the feature flag fix instead for a safer roll-forward.

Maria: Thanks — assigning followups: Ajay (bisect + tcpdump), Sophia (deep IO profiling), Tyler (CI perf job run), Kevin (revert PR monitor). Will update here once we have pcap + bisect result. :thumbsup:

Maria: Initial bisect points to commit c3f9a2b -> change set includes `EventStream::write_header` and `ToolCall::handshake` small refactors. Next step is a micro-repro that toggles header padding.

Ajay: Micro-repro confirmed: toggling padding off reduces p99 by ~22% and toolcall handshake time back to baseline. Confirmed in staging with same workload.

Maria: OK let's keep rollout on hold, merge the feature-flag patch, and then re-run perf CI. If CI looks good, we can re-deploy with flag off and do a gradual opt-in.

deploy-bot: Revert PR #3130 merged to release branch at 2026-03-18T12:05Z.

Maria: Follow-up ticket created: PERF-987 "Eventstream padded header causes small-write i/o regression" with links to pcap, bisect output, and revert PR.

Kevin: Good catch, team. We'll do a proper async flush + aggregate header write in the next iteration so we don't regress tail latency.
